analysis.title: Phillips Edison & Co. (PECO): 3Q26 First Take: Core FFOPS beat and (smaller) raise with record renewal spreads
key_insights: PECO reported Core 3Q26 FFOPS of $0.71, 3% above the GS/FactSet consensus of $0.69 and +9.2% y/y. The beat vs GS estimate came from higher base rent, lower bad debt and lower G&A than expected.

Economic occupancy reached 97.2% (+30bps q/q, +20bps y/y). Leased rate for the full portfolio was 97.5% (+20bps q/q, -10bps y/y). GS says economic occupancy continues to strengthen but has some remaining upside.

Total leasing spreads (new, renewal and options) were +16.2% in 3Q26 vs +15.1% over the TTM. New lease spreads were +26.3%, below the +32.8% TTM. Renewal spreads were +25.2%, a record and 330bps above the 21.9% TTM. Comparable inline renewal spreads were a record 24.2%.
Bad debt was about 71bps of revenue in 3Q26 (2Q26: 73bps, FY24 and FY25 each about 80bps), near the low end of management's 70-80bps run-rate range. PECO cut its 2026 bad debt guidance range by 4.5%.
Same-store NOI growth was +5.3% in 3Q. The larger 9.2% Core FFO growth reflects PECO's active acquisition strategy.

PECO raised FY26 Core FFO guidance by two cents at the low end to $2.75-$2.79. The new $2.77 midpoint implies 6.5% y/y growth vs 5.4% in the initial guidance and 7.0% growth in 2025. GS FY26 Core FFO estimate is at the $2.77 midpoint.

The guidance raise included SS NOI growth of 3.5%-4% (from 3.4%-4%), a smaller collectibility headwind of $4.5-$6mn (from $4-$7mn), lower interest expense of $116-$120mn (from $117-$127mn) and higher non-cash revenue of $22-$24mn (from $21-$23mn). GS views these as generally high quality drivers with positive implications for 2027.

PECO closed a $350mn three-year term loan at SOFR +80bps, 30bps lower than the term loan it repaid. $175mn was drawn at closing and used to repay a $161.8mn term loan and revolver balances. The other $175mn is available to draw on or before 4/21/27, and an accordion allows up to $450mn more. GS views it positively for flexibility on acquisitions and avoiding refinancing headwinds.

3Q pro rata acquisitions were $181.8mn across three shopping centers (two grocery-anchored, one unanchored) plus land/outparcels, the highest quarterly volume since 4Q23. Dispositions were $87.1mn. YTD acquisition cap rate is 6.5% vs 6.1% for dispositions, a spread that narrowed to 40bps from 80bps at 1H26.
FY property acquisition guidance of $600-$700mn is unchanged from the 10/1/26 update and up from $500-$600mn at 2Q26 earnings.

After quarter-end PECO expanded and extended by 10 years its Grocery Retail Partners I JV with Northwestern Mutual, to acquire 13 grocery-anchored centers at about $377.5mn across eight states. GS expects PECO to recycle the capital into higher growth assets.
The active expansion/redevelopment pipeline rose to $85.7mn from $82.0mn. Projected redevelopment yields rose to 13%-25% from 11%-20%. Expansion yields were unchanged at 7%-10%.

Net debt/EBITDA was 5.2x annualized at 3Q26, slightly up from 5.1x at 6/30/26. SNO spread of 30bps is 30bps below PECO's historical average, though GS says SNO is less meaningful for PECO because its leases are for smaller spaces with a short signing-to-opening gap.

GS is Buy-rated on PECO with a $44.00 12-month price target (17.9x Q5-Q8 AFFO) vs a $38.60 price, 14.0% upside. GS expects PECO could outperform on Tuesday 10/27 and had flagged PECO in its retail preview as a likely FY26 FFO and SS NOI guidance raise.
GS will tour PECO assets in Atlanta with the CFO, IR and regional team on Monday, November 16, the week of Nareit.

market_movers.rationale: Core FFOPS beat, guidance raise and record renewal spreads. GS likes PECO's ability to drive earnings growth through same-store and acquisition channels.

sector_views.rationale: PECO's same-store occupancy is high vs peers (BRX, KIM, MAC, SKT, SPG) for anchor and small shop space, with strong leasing spreads and low bad debt.

earnings_insights: PECO Core 3Q26 FFOPS $0.71 reported, vs GS/FactSet consensus est $0.69, +9.2% y/y.
FY26 Core FFO guidance raised to $2.75-$2.79 (midpoint $2.77, +6.5% y/y), from a low end two cents lower. GS FY26 FFOPS estimate is $2.77 per the text, and $2.76 in the GS forecast table.
SS NOI growth was +5.3% in 3Q26. FY26 SS NOI growth guidance is now 3.5%-4%, from 3.4%-4%.

Q3 earnings call topics GS will watch: drivers of the guidance raise vs June, 4Q26 moving pieces, reduced disposition guidance, the Northwestern Mutual JV contribution timing, new lease spread moderation, funding costs and bad debt watchlist.
risk_factors: Deterioration in the open air retail environment.
Higher retailer bankruptcies or tenant credit headwinds, including struggling national chains and local retailers.
Lower than expected occupancy and leasing spreads.
Higher than expected interest rates and a higher cost of capital, including a weaker disposition market.
Lower acquisition volumes, yields and IRRs, and lower development volumes or returns.
Lower interest in strip center concepts.
